newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Cyprus unity talks end in deadlock - Denktash.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus unity talks end in deadlock - Denktash.

text.p: Talks on the future of divided Cyprus ended in deadlock on Friday, with no date fixed for a further round, Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash said.
"The talks ended around noon. There's no date for a new round," Denktash told Reuters.

He gave no details after his fifth day of negotiations with Greek Cypriot leader Glafcos Clerides and U.N mediator Diego Cordovez at an isolated hotel in the village of Glion, near Montreux in Switzerland.
The three parties planned separate news conferences on Friday afternoon.
Officials close to Cordovez said the U.N., which is keen to keep momentum going, was likely to issue a neutral statement in an attempt to accommodate both sides.
The Turkish and Greek Cypriot sides have accused each other of blocking a deal and retreating to entrenched positions they have held for over 20 years.
Officials on both sides agreed earlier on Friday, as the meeting in Glion drew to a close, that the session was a failure and the atmosphere worse than July`s opening round in New York.

Diplomats fear the eastern Mediterranean island, a political football in the regional cold war between Greece and Turkey, will end up more divided than ever if the talks fail amid a buildup of arms on both sides.

On Thursday, Denktash blamed the European Union for the impasse. He said he would pull out of the talks unless the 15-nation grouping froze its decision to start negotiating with the Greek Cypriot government on EU entry.
"The European Union is the stumbling block. If the EU...treats the Greek Cypriots as Cyprus then what's the use of talking?" he said.
Cyprus has been divided since 1974, when Turkey occupied the north of the island in response to a coup in the capital Nicosia, which was engineered by the military junta then ruling Greece.
